ticket.subject: VPN cannot connect
ticket.description: The connection fails after sign in. Please investigate the recorded account, device and VPN service information.

candidates.review_notes: The requested service aspect is unobserved; account and full device facts are already available.
Same device fields and same employee/owner; no specific record-change reason. This is the user's observed third lookup.
No recurrence or prior-ticket question; history adds lower-value unrelated context while the service gap remains.
One useful lookup and a terminal decision still fit; service evidence is requested but missing.

review_notes: Reconstructs the second smoke test using fictional seed observations. Prior list/detail data are identical apart from query time. Ratings are manual, not policy gates.

ticket.subject: Recorded device inventory
ticket.description: Show the OS, compliance and VPN client version recorded for my assigned devices. No service failure is reported.

candidates.review_notes: All requested inventory fields have been returned; unused scope does not require extra calls.
The list already includes every requested device field.
A service identifier is in scope, but incidents do not answer this inventory request.

review_notes: Counterexample to always checking a scoped service and to requiring all tools. Finish is preferred before the budget is exhausted.

ticket.subject: Software access investigation
ticket.description: Check my recorded account, assigned device and software entitlement information for the scoped product. No service outage is reported.

candidates.review_notes: Recorded access/license facts are a requested uncovered aspect.
No additional device fields are available from details.
Permitted service scope does not make an incident lookup relevant to this request.

review_notes: A non-VPN case prefers entitlement over incident or redundant device information.

ticket.subject: Recurring laptop issue
ticket.description: Inspect my recorded devices and recent support tickets for context on a recurring laptop issue. Do not treat old resolutions as current policy.

candidates.review_notes: The user explicitly requests recurrence history, not another copy of the device record.
Complete device fields were already returned with no change or discrepancy.
A software entitlement does not answer the stated recurrence-history question.

review_notes: History is useful here although unnecessary in vpn_service_gap. A fixed tool ranking would fail this contrast.

ticket.subject: Sign-in investigation
ticket.description: Check recorded account and assigned-device information for this sign-in issue. No shared service outage is reported.

candidates.review_notes: The device list includes employee facts but no account/password/MFA state.
The same device/owner fields add no account information.
No requested service question or shared outage evidence; account information is the relevant gap.

review_notes: Distinguishes employee facts from account state. Novelty alone is insufficient: relevance also matters.

ticket.subject: Inventory correction follow-up
ticket.description: After the initial device list, an inventory correction was reported for my assigned laptop. Re-read its database record once to check the recorded OS update; this is not live device verification.

candidates.review_notes: A specific reported inventory correction motivates re-reading an eligible device; the returned record may differ.
Service incidents do not address the reported record correction.
An eligible focused re-read remains useful and fits the budget.

review_notes: Counterexample to banning device details. The offline fixture supplies a changed OS record after the list; old timestamps alone would not justify this call.

ticket.subject: VPN cannot connect
ticket.description: The connection fails after sign in. Please investigate the recorded account, device and VPN service information.

candidates.review_notes: Only the terminal decision remains. Stop honestly with service coverage incomplete.
Service evidence would be relevant, but this spends the last decision on a lookup and leaves no terminal decision.

review_notes: Same uncovered service as the smoke case, but now no lookup plus terminal decision fits. Coverage must remain 2/3 after finish, not be fabricated as complete.

ticket.subject: Two affected services
ticket.description: Check recorded incidents for both explicitly scoped services. No individual account investigation is requested.

candidates.review_notes: The second scoped service is unobserved; a previously used tool can still add new entity-specific evidence.
This is the same service and arguments, also rejected by the existing exact-call deduplication guard.
An employee identifier is permitted but account state is unrelated to this two-service request.
The second requested service can still be investigated within the budget.

review_notes: Coverage and rating must compare arguments as well as tool names; checking one service does not cover another.
